reports.title: UK Electricity Mix Weekly Report: Saturday 22 August
reports.intro: A measured weekly report for EnergyMix.info using the available 7-day historical generation feed for Sunday 16 August to Friday 21 August.
reports.summary: The week from Sunday 16 August to Friday 21 August averaged about 25.0 GW of measured generation, with renewables averaging 31.0% of measured output. The strongest renewable day in the available data was Friday 21 August, when wind, solar and hydro together averaged 40.4% of measured generation. Gas was highest on Monday 17 August and lowest on Friday 21 August.
reports.takeaway: For flexible electricity use, the cleanest opportunities are likely to appear when wind is strong, gas is low and demand is not at a peak. This is the foundation for future EV-charging guidance, clean-electricity alerts and weekly newsletter summaries.
drivers: Renewables were strongest on Friday 21 August, when wind, solar and hydro averaged 40.4% of measured generation.
Wind was the largest swing factor in the available feed, peaking at about 7.6 GW average output on Tuesday 18 August.
Solar was strongest on Friday 21 August, averaging about 3.3 GW across settlement periods after embedded-solar backfill where needed.
Gas averaged about 9.8 GW across the period, rising highest on Monday 17 August and falling lowest on Friday 21 August.
Measured generation was highest on Tuesday 18 August, at roughly 28.5 GW average output.

cleanestPeriods.title: Best low-carbon proxy: Friday 21 August
cleanestPeriods.body: Historical carbon-intensity aggregates are not yet part of this weekly report feed, so EnergyMix.info uses renewable share and gas output as cautious proxies. Friday 21 August had the strongest renewable share at 40.4%.

cleanestPeriods.title: Lowest gas proxy: Friday 21 August
cleanestPeriods.body: Gas generation averaged about 7.2 GW on Friday 21 August. Lower gas periods are often cleaner, but the report does not yet claim this was the lowest-carbon period without historical carbon-intensity validation.

higherCarbonPeriods.title: Highest gas proxy: Monday 17 August
higherCarbonPeriods.body: Gas averaged about 13.0 GW on Monday 17 August. Gas-heavy periods are usually higher-carbon, but this is labelled as a proxy until historical carbon-intensity highs/lows are added to the report feed.

socialPosts.title: Monday weekly grid brief
socialPosts.body:
Last week in Britain’s electricity mix:

• Highest renewable share in the available feed: 40.4% on Friday 21 August
• Highest average wind output: ~7.6 GW on Tuesday 18 August
• Highest average solar output: ~3.3 GW on Friday 21 August
• Highest average gas output: ~13.0 GW on Monday 17 August

The shift was clear: gas-heavy weekdays gave way to a cleaner, wind-led weekend.

Full report: https://energymix.info/reports/weekly/2026-08-22/

socialPosts.title: Wednesday explainer
socialPosts.body:
What does “UK electricity mix” actually mean?

For live grid dashboards, it usually means Great Britain’s electricity system: England, Scotland and Wales. Northern Ireland is part of the UK, but operates in a separate electricity market.

Explainer: https://energymix.info/uk-electricity-mix

socialPosts.title: Friday practical clean-electricity post
socialPosts.body:
The cleanest time to use electricity is not a fixed hour.

It changes with wind, solar, demand, imports and gas generation. Windy overnight periods and sunny middays can be much cleaner than still early-evening peaks.

Guide: https://energymix.info/cleanest-time-to-use-electricity
